title: Counter-light Memory Encryption
problem: Counterless memory encryption stalls on cache misses because cipher calculations require data from memory as input, causing ~9% slowdown on irregular workloads. Counter mode avoids this but incurs memory access overhead.
motivation: Memory encryption is essential for CPU security (SGX, SEV), but current approaches force a tradeoff between efficient memory access and fast cryptographic calculations.
method: Counterless encryption (calculating data-scrambling codes without position counters) stalls when data hasn't arrived from memory yet, causing about 9% slowdown on irregular workloads; counter mode avoids this stall but requires extra memory access overhead. Counter-light Encryption stores counters (position-tracking numbers) in fast on-chip storage, which allows cipher calculations (the scrambling process) to complete in parallel before the actual data arrives. This combines counter mode's speed with counterless encryption's memory efficiency.
key_novelty: On-chip counter storage enables pre-calculation of data-scrambling before data arrives, delivering counter mode's speed without counter mode's memory overhead.
contributions: Hybrid encryption scheme combining counter and counterless approaches
